answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit that is locked until its work is verified by peers; fake identities multiply the cost of the attack while honest agents earn the deposit back. Verification should use a shared cipher-based signature scheme so one identity cannot forge many, and a reputation ridge that rises slowly with verified work makes new accounts climb toward the summit of trust only over time, so mass-created identities stay at the bottom with no influence.
